text: Working with APIs is an important skill for modern developers. An API allows two programs to communicate with each other. To get data, your application sends HTTP requests to a server. Most APIs return information in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before you can use an API, you usually need authentication, such as an API key, to prove who you are. Be careful about rate limits, because servers only allow a certain number of requests per minute. Finally, always add error handling to your code. Networks fail and servers return errors, so your application should handle these problems gracefully instead of crashing.
